x: Barden (Sheffield) with A. Morrison bringing the Bels home in sixth place.

On Nov 9th at Wimbledon, Alan Morrison and Roger Hudson---both members of Belgrave Harriers!---both members of the Aristotle school!---both won their Championship races, Intermediate and Junior!---both set new course records!

Alan Morrison, Ken Redwood and David Cocks were together in the forties and Chris Steer near the seventy mark. The leaders had separated from the field as they came down the farm yard and turned sharp right to cross over the plough.
Bruce and Shippen were lethargic and Lennie Bishop faded after a promising start; but young Alan Morrison should feel encouraged, performing as he did in this his first race over the distance.
For the second consecutive year Alan Black produced fastest time, but bouquets should really go to two of Tom Carter's protegés, Alan Morrison (Youth) and Tony Fairclough (Junior).

Belgrave were fielding the strongest team and the first leg was entrusted to Alan Morrison, who brought us home in 9th place - somewhat disappointing but nevertheless a good effort in the face of such strong opposition.
Our first leg runner, Alan Morrison, followed the pattern of the previous week and handed over once again to Ken Redwood in 9th position. Ken then ran a "blinder" to take us up to third.
Before long however, Alan Morrison was spiked, an unfortunate accident which sorely affected his running and consequently he was forced to drop several places.

Alan Morrison gave away a mere second on the next stage, and with Ken Redwood increasing our lead by a further ½ minute on the third leg 'Noddy' Edwards set off on the final stage with a very comfortable lead.
Winner Alan Morrison (4:37.2) was followed by Steer (4:39.0) 3rd, Bicourt (4:40.0)-and still a Youth,- 4th, and Redwood, Angus and Satchell making it 6 in 9.
The mile was something of a humdinger with Alan Morrison and Chris Steer battling all the way up the straight with Alan just getting the verdict and John Bicourt coming in well to take third place.
Good performances were put up by Alan Morrison (115th) and Fred Paget(148th) and Keith Angus a new member showed great promise in finishing 170th.

Allan Morrison dropped from equal 3rd to 9th over the last two laps but is fast making the grade. If there had been a handicap in conjunction, this would very likely have been won by Trevor Hart whose 15:36 was a personal best.
At the end of Stage 1 fourth place seemed little more than a dream, for Alan Morrison had a disastrous day finishing last of the 12 runners and nearly 2 mins down on the leaders.
Alan Morrison, Dave Cocks, and Jack Hampshire have been other regular members of the junior team and have had good and indifferent runs alike.

Dave Cocks and Alan Morrison were now in the twenties and it was touch and go between Windsor and ourselves. Fairclough kept his 3rd place to the end, but the others lost a few very valuable places and Windsor pipped us by 8 points.

Alan Morrison also faded, but his 107th was relatively better; whilst Dave Cock's 145th was particularly disappointing. Bob Brown, despite a heavily bandaged hand came down from Derby to complete our six, and although losing a shoe into the bargain finished a gallant, but tired, 372.
After a fast start, Charlie brought our 'A' team in 10th followed closely by Alan Morrison, 1[illegible]th, for the 'B' team. City of Rochester and SLH led at this point.

The rest of our scoring team were all high up in the field but nothing could have beaten Hercules AC who won the team event easily,even without one of their star men - Dave Holt. Howard Satchell nearly caused an upset when he was only narrowly beaten by Alan Morrison;thus just missing a team medal.
With Brian Nott and Alan Morrison representing the Banks on this occasion and finishing 3rd and 5th into the bargain, Belgrave only scraped home in the match result by their 6th man's position.
Alan Morrison helped our score along with a now regular sub 2 mins "half" (1:59.3) finishing second and O'Hara and Thorpe took first two places in the mile with 4:16 and 4:19:7.
87 finished,110 started,20 teams closed in. Alan Morrison and Brian Nott running for Barclays and Westminster Banks were 29th and 16th respectively with times of 42:43 and 40:57.
Once again Alan Morrison was 2nd in the half; this time with 1:59.7. Our other runners-up were Don Maclean in the mile (4:29.5) and Tony Fairclough in the 3 miles (14:44.4).
The ever-reliable Jackie Hampshire was our next man (148) followed by Dave Cocks and Alan Morrison, both below their best. A disappointing points total of 673 gave us a lowly 28th team placing.

John was second in the same time and Alan Morrison,showing a startling and welcome return to form,came third with 1:58.0 . The Mile provided some good performances but no-one could match Laurie O'hara's devastating finish.
Match Result: Met.Police W.C. 60pts BELGRAVE H 76pts. Handicap: 1.J.Wilson 35:42, 2.A.Morrison 35:53, 3.J.Baker 36:03
A friendly atmosphere prevailed in our opening match of the season at Epsom, with our opponents having a Belgravian flavour in the form of Alan Morrison, Geoff Pearson and Stan Bradshaw.
This resulted in a good win for Howard Satchell with John Martin, who ran exceptionally well, second and the fast improving Alan Morrison third.
